Subject: NimbusX-2.1b — spike in 5xx/timeouts for streaming requests (observed 09:00 UTC)

Team,

We started seeing a spike in 5xx (502/504) and client timeouts on NimbusX-2.1b for long-streaming requests beginning ~08:55 UTC. Error rate on ingress for that model is ~6x baseline and affects customers using streaming + long context (>8k tokens).

Immediate observations: 
- Cluster: us-west-2-nimbus-pool-3
- Symptom: backend worker processes reporting KV cache misses and OOM-related restarts; load average up on a subset of GPU nodes
- Impacting: BlueStone Analytics (streaming embeddings + transcription), a few smaller demo customers

I attached a short sample of the error traces for your reference (initial-error-sample.log).

Immediate asks:
1) Marissa: can you pull cfg/quant/commit history for NimbusX variants deployed in that pool (last 48h)?
2) Dylan: can infra check node-level OOMs, driver resets, and gpu-mem fragmentation metrics for the pool?
3) Steph: prep a short customer note (one-paragraph) we can send to BlueStone while we triage. Keep it transparent but short — we want to acknowledge and provide next steps.

I'll gate any customer-facing message until we confirm whether this is config/quantization related or a runtime regression.

Thanks,
Irene

Subject: Re: NimbusX-2.1b — spike in 5xx/timeouts for streaming requests (observed 09:00 UTC)

Irene — quick triage notes: 
- Deployment diff shows a variant promotion rolled 46m ago: nimbusx-2.1b-quant-a -> a2. The promotion included an aggressive KV cache shrinker that was meant to reduce mem pressure for short requests.
- Node checks: Dylan confirmed 3 nodes showing repeated process restarts and driver resets; enriched logs in s3 path: s3://redwood-ops-logs/nimbusx/2026/12/01/trace-9876.json
- Hypothesis: cache shrinker + long streaming sequences -> excessive KV cache churn + OOMs causing worker restart cascade and 5xxs.

Next steps I'm executing now: 
- Rolling back variant a2 to previous config on the affected pool (started at 10:18 UTC).
- Increasing autoscaler burst on that dedicated pool to absorb retry pressure for 20m.
- Capturing heap/kv stats during rollback window.

If rollback doesn't stabilize within 15–20m we'll flip affected customer routes to fallback model (nimbusx-2.1b-safe) and send the customer note.

Marissa
Marissa Cole

Redwood Inference

Subject: Service interruption affecting NimbusX-2.1b streaming — current status and mitigation

Aaron / BlueStone team,

We detected an elevated rate of 5xx errors and client-side streaming timeouts impacting some requests to NimbusX-2.1b beginning ~08:55 UTC today. We know this has affected your streaming transcription jobs; sincerely sorry for the disruption.

What we have done so far (12:00 UTC):
- Identified a promoted configuration variant (nimbusx-2.1b-quant-a2) that introduced a more aggressive KV cache shrinker; this interacted poorly with long streaming sequences and triggered worker restarts on a subset of nodes.
- Rolled back the variant on the affected pool and increased autoscaler burst to handle retry traffic.
- If traffic doesn't stabilize within 20m, we will automatically route your requests to the fallback model (nimbusx-2.1b-safe) to restore availability with minimal quality difference.

What we need from you:
- If you can share the highest-impact request ids or a short example (trace IDs) that hit during 08:55–09:30 UTC it will help confirmation (we collected traces under trace-9876).

Proposed short-term mitigation (we're executing now):
- Keep your clients on current endpoint for now; we will flip to fallback only if errors persist.
- Expect a stabilization update by 12:30 UTC.

Attachments: mitigation-commands.txt (commands we executed for rollback)

I'll follow up with a postmortem summary once we've validated full recovery.

Best,
Irene Choi
Sr. Technical Program Manager

Subject: NimbusX-2.1b — stabilization confirmed and RCA summary (INC-4567)

Team / BlueStone (cc above),

Final update and short RCA:

Timeline (summary):
- 08:55 UTC 2026-12-01: elevated 5xx/timeouts observed for long streaming sessions
- 09:08 UTC: customer reports (BlueStone) of incomplete stream bs-trans-4421
- 10:18 UTC: rollback of nimbusx-2.1b-quant-a2 initiated on the affected pool
- 10:30–11:00 UTC: error rate declined to baseline and worker restarts subsided
- 12:20 UTC: system-level stabilization confirmed; no further customer-impacting 5xxs recorded

Root cause: an aggressive KV cache shrinker introduced in the quantized variant promoted yesterday caused excessive KV re-computation under long continuous decode (streaming) workloads. The added CPU/allocator pressure led to intermittent OOMs and worker restarts which manifested as 5xxs and client timeouts.

Corrective actions (short-term):
- Reverted the promoted variant immediately and restored the previous cache sizing profile (complete, 10:18 UTC).
- Added a temporary guardrail to block aggressive shrinker flags on streaming-enabled routes.
- Increased autoscaler burst capacity for the affected pool and added retry budget controls for streaming RPCs.

Longer-term actions (planned):
- Engineering: introduce a streaming-aware KV cache mode that diffs cache policies by request type (ETA: Q1 2027).
- Release: add pre-promotion safety tests for streaming workloads to model onboarding checks.
- Ops: automate rollback trigger if worker restart rate > 1/min for any pool (INC-4567 ticket created).

Customer remediation: we provided BlueStone the fallback route and didn't need to flip it. BlueStone confirmed degraded but acceptable behavior during the window and will share logs for bs-trans-4421.

Postmortem doc attached (nimbusx-rca-20261202.pdf) and INC-4567 links are in related_links above.

Thanks to everyone who jumped in — Marissa/Dylan/Steph, please file the follow-up PRs for the guardrail and streaming test.

Irene
